text: After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, rose up to deliver Israel. He lived in Shamir, in the hill country of Ephraim.
He judged Israel twenty-three years, and then he died and was buried in Shamir.
After him rose Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel twenty-two years.
He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty towns in the land of Gilead, which to this day are called Havvoth-jair.*

versions.text: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty towns in the land of Gilead, which to this day are called Havvoth-jair.
versions.explanation: A brief footnote explaining that Havvoth-jair means 'the settlements of Jair' would help hearers understand the name; the Hebrew also contains a wordplay between 'donkeys' (ʿayarim) and 'towns' (ʿayarim) that could be noted.

text: Then Jair died and was buried in Kamon.

Again the Israelites did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. They served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the Ammonites, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandoned the LORD and no longer served him.
So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hands of the Philistines and the Ammonites.
That year they shattered and crushed the Israelites, and for eighteen years they oppressed all the Israelites beyond the Jordan, in the land of the Amorites in Gilead.

versions.text: That year they crushed and oppressed the Israelites, and for eighteen years they oppressed all the Israelites beyond the Jordan, in the land of the Amorites in Gilead.
versions.explanation: The word 'oppressed' occurs twice in close succession, which sounds repetitive when read aloud. Using 'shattered and crushed' better reflects the Hebrew word pair (רעץ / רצץ) and avoids the echo.

text: The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to make war on Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, and Israel was in dire distress.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD: "We have sinned against you. We have abandoned our God and served the Baals."
And the LORD said to the Israelites: "Did I not save you from Egypt, from the Amorites, from the Ammonites, and from the Philistines?

versions.text: And the LORD said to the Israelites: "Was it not I who saved you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, and the Philistines?
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has 'from Egypt' (the nation/land), not 'the Egyptians'; the parallel series of 'from...' phrases also reads with better rhythm and matches the Hebrew structure.

text: When the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites oppressed you, and you cried out to me, I saved you from their hand.
But you have abandoned me and served other gods. Therefore I will deliver you no more.
Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. Let them save you in your time of distress."
But the Israelites said to the LORD, "We have sinned. Do to us whatever seems good to you—only deliver us this day, we beg you."
So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD, and he could no longer bear Israel's misery.
The Ammonites were called to arms and camped in Gilead, and the Israelites assembled and camped at Mizpah.
The people, the leaders of Gilead, said to one another, "Whoever takes the lead in fighting the Ammonites will be head over all who live in Gilead."
